President Bongbong Marcos Jr. versus all ghost, substandard, questionable flood control projects

I was stuck in traffic for three hours within Quezon City because of the flooding yesterday — after a sudden downpour of rain. Reports say that was 5 days worth of rain dumped in just one hour. 

Although we don’t know this fact yet, the sentiment of my driver was understandable. He was airing out  the common sentiments against the DPWH and corrupt officials. Asking if billions of money were allocated for this purpose, why are they still experiencing this? I reminded him that it was the President himself who exposed this — the call was from his critics, it was the President himself who wants to end all these corrupt practices. 

I am sure that the President is fully aware that his call to hold all the people responsible for the dubious flood control projects should be held accountable will hurt people. It will expose the inefficiencies and negligence of DPWH — but seeing the flood victims himself, consequences be damned. Corrupt practices must stop.

We are at a very high time when corrupt officials and contractors are now thinking twice before doing anything bad — this for me is already a win.

Love them or hate them — but we all know that the Marcoses are known for their good and long lasting projects, a lot of the things we use now are from decades ago. In Ilocos Norte, it is known that the young Marcos is strict with things like this — talking to the locals, Majority Floor Leader Marcos made sure that the solar panels in public school can withstand even strong typhoon signals. Giving them light and power in times not just on the school days but also when they need to evacuate. That is also the same in every project in his district.

You could only just imagine the anger and disappointment of President Marcos during his ocular inspections. Thinking if he has more time, if only he could micromanage this (not ideal and should not happen) — things would be better.

I agree with most of you, DPWH is responsible and Secretary Bonoan dropped the ball. No doubt in my mind about this. But I still don’t know if he should be removed or demand that he fix this —

Although I think Senator Marcoleta will not touch anything close to the 51 Billion flood control budget of the Dutertes in one district, nor the campaign funds donated by contractors to his beloved Senate President and Majority Floor Leader… I still support any investigation that will help the President. 

But just to be sure, I am also glad that the more credible investigation in the House of Representatives is about to start on Tuesday — the InfraComm!
